entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 29823 (2223 miles travelled). Used up all Dracks. Left Greece. 1pm entered Turkey. Mileage = 29898 miles (2298 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30025 (2425 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Last night, just out of Xanthis, we went down a road in between fields to camp, lots of peasant farmers passed us, there were lots of mosquitos. We are driving to Turkey and Istanbul, we are seeing lots of storks in big parties, and other migrating birds. When we reached Istanbul, we found our campsite, it is very nice and clean, it has hot water - free! We ate out in the camp restaurant. I had siskebab with chips, and lemonade. When we got back to the van we had a delicious melon, which we bought at a market.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We woke up at 7 o’clock. Me and Helena went blackberry picking. I saw a spider about as big as a house spider - it had yellow and black horizontal stripes on its abdomen and legs, the head was a light grey. We saw a flock of migrating storks. We took some pictures of them. Denise and I stalked them!

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Into Istanbul on Minibus. REAL experience - squashed, terrifying and friendly. Went to covered Bazaar. Saw coppersmiths, leather etc, some carpets. Girls bought onyx pillbox and pestle and mortar. Lunch just outside bazaar - good. Walked to Underground Cisterns - v. impressive. Then to Topkapi Palace - jewels were unbelievable. Pretty ??. Bought some ?? reserve.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: I hardly slept at all last night because of the mosquitoes. We are now going to see (Istanbul) the City. When at last we found the right Minibus, we only just squeezed in. When we got out, went and walked past some shops, we got lost, but finally made our way to the big covered bazaar. There were lots of leather coats and bags for sale. There were also shops selling onyx, I looked round and finally I found a pestle and mortar that I looked, the man said 100L as a specially low price, but we bargained down to 75L. I also tried on some coats and jackets, but I didn’t buy any. When we came out it was raining, and we went and had siskebab for lunch. We went to see the big underground cistern, it had 336 pillars, and it was an emergency water supply for the City, it is not used anymore and is only about 1 metre deep. It was about 1400 years old. When we finished we walked up to a big palace, it had belonged to a long succession of Sultans and was now a kind of museum, there were some magnificent plates and bowls etc and the jewel room was fantastic. There were some enormous jewels, emeralds in particular. Helena and I went on a guided tour of the Harem, it was enormous. We came out, lost ourselves (again) had a meal, and finally found ourselves back in the minibus place again. We found one going to the campsite and again squeezed ourselves on, we were even more squashed up, but it was unbelievable, we already had about 30 people, the bus just seated 20, and during the course of our journey, about 5 more somehow squashed in.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At the campsite we had a swim, in the rather shallow pool and then H and I had a shower, in the middle of which there was a blackout, it only lasted about 5 min. and then stopped. Mum and Dad told us about a stork that had fallen on to an electric wire and been electrocuted (killed, dead). That was probably the cause of the lights going out.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We had breakfast and did our diaries then we got the 6 minibus. It was fast. The driver spoke in English to me. We stopped near the Bazaar, we went in, it was quite crowded. There were jewellers, copper, onyx and leather shops. Helena got a small oval box, gold with an onyx lid. Denise got an onyx pestle and mortar. Then we went to Topkapi Palace. It was made by the Turkish Sultans. In the Treasury there were two hugh identical candlesticks each with 6666 diamonds for the 6666 verses of the Koran and they weighed together 272000 grams!

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: 272000 grams! One emerald weighed 3700 grams! One diamond weighed 9.8 grams. In the harem, there were at one time 400 ladies.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Today we took a minibus to Istanbul. We passed a bazaar then we went to a square. Daddy looked at the map, we were at the University. Afterwards, we walked to a covered bazaar. We passed lots of coats then we came to a shop which sold pillboxes. I saw one I liked. I bought it for 50 lira. It has gold walls with flowers printed on it, the stone in the lid is green with brown - it is called onyx. Went to a palace (Topkapi). Denise and I went on a guided tour of the Harem. The Harem is the place where the Sultan keeps his 400 or more wives. If his wives fall in love with anyone else, they get their heads chopped off.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30195 (2595 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Today we went in to Istanbul in the van, and we visited some Mosques, the first was not very nice, but the second Mosque, the Blue Mosque was much nicer, and we had to take our shoes off, because the Muslims put their heads on the floor. After lunch we drove off and crossed the bridge into Asia.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Went to the Blue Mosque. There were lots of tiles, mostly blue. The Moslims pray 5 times a day. In the mosque you are not allowed to wear shoes. The floor was one mass of carpets. We went to a park and had lunch.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Me and Helena made a Bivouac in a pit out of stones.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to the Blue Mosque. It was nice. We had to take off our shoes before going inside. The muslims pray five times every day. The ceiling had pretty patterns. It’s called the Blue Mosque because the tiles on the walls are blue.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30206 (2606 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove into Bursa, and at length found the ‘Yesil’ (green) Mosque. We had to remove our shoes and Mum and I covered our heads. It was very beautiful, a nice man took us round, and up to the minaret, where tourists weren’t really allowed, it was all very old. Went to and old and new brass shop. I bought a little brass jar, we bargain all our things down. We also passed a caravanserai, where camel trains used to rest and sell etc.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Finished Bivouac and did diaries. We went to the council Mosque. We climbed a pinnacle - we were not meant to. Dad took a photo. It was once used by the Turkish government.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: The Green or Council mosque has libraries - each 400 years old. Some people were praying. The Sultan and a few of the harem used to be there.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to the Green Mosque. We went up the minaret where tourists are not allowed to go. Afterwards, we went shopping and got a red jewel, a pair of clogs and a necklace.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30357 (2757 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Spent night near Erdeck by sea. Lots of olives. Photo of Bird of Prey, Women in fields etc. Through v.large fields of sunflowers, maize etc. Also hills of purple heather and beehives. Saw 3 bears, muzzled walking alond road. Photo dancing bears. Saw ?? ?? ?? his house in 1357. Almost entirely hollow but still alive. Photo of camels etc near Troy. Stopped off a side road - 2 girls D & H’s age bought us ?? We gave them some peppers ?? ?? ??. Troy.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped near the sea, but didn’t swim. Drove along and when we stopped for lunch, a nice girl came and gave us two melons, she had her younger sister with her, they gave us some more things, and we gave them some sweets. We drove on and found a nice view across the sea to Europe, and asked the way to Troy, we received directions and went on our way. When we arrived, almost the first thing we saw was an enormous wooden horse, we were able to climb up into it, like the Greeks. We went all round the old walls, a lot was left to the imagination though. There were 9 layers of the city, the earliest dating from about 3000 BC.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Troy. There was a wooden horse, real size,. We climbed inside - it was huge. I had two ideas of the ruined city. (Pic)

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to Troy. There is a famous wooden horse. I will try to draw it. We have been inside it. (Pic)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30512 (2912 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Photo of some travelling gypsies.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Pergammon v.g. Punctured front left tyre. Ran out of gas.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Last night we camped in some pine trees, and some Poles came and camped next to us, they only spoke German and Russian though. When we left in the morning we found that we had a flat tyre. F and I played Scrabble while Mum and Dad mended the wheel. In the afternoon we went to visit the Asklepion of Pergammon. It was a very old Hospital, situated there because of the springs, there was an old Library and Amphitheatre as well. A long tunnel ran underground with holes in the roof, patients used to have to run through the tunnel, while priests shouted down the holes “get well, get well”. We also climbed up to the Acropolis, it was on a very steep hill, then we came down to a town and ate out, everything covered with pepper though.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Today we went to Pergamon. It was a citadel on a high steep hill. It was dry stoned wall. There is a huge Arsenal for amo. You could see the viaducts for water. There was a big Amphitheatre with lots of stairs - it was very steep. We climbed down - I went first. There were some big lizards and some little lizards - I chased them. Then we went to a Restaurant - everything was peppery so we didn’t like it much.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Today was a load of rubbish! We went to the Asclepion at Pergammon and walked along the sacred road to the sacred tunnel where people who are ill go. They run through it and priests shouted “get well!” through holes in the roof. The city was on top of a mountain.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30658 (3058 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Photo of view along Pergamon Izmir Rd.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Stayed Izmir ?? Camp. H runny tummy - gave her ??. Seemed to clear.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We got up very early and drove to Izmir, where we had breakfast, we are in a campsite. There are free gas rings, so for lunch, nice and clean after a shower, H and I cooked pancakes, they were delicious. In the afternoon we made a tent over the drying racks, with duvets etc. At night we had spaghetti and on the way back from the van, I caught a frog, it was about 1½” long, when not stretched out jumping, it was very slimy and slippery to hold. There were lots of cats as well.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 30743 (3143 miles travelled) - At Kuzadasi

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the afternoon, we went to see some ruins, some were very well preserved. We drove on, and found a nice beach, the water was super. At Kusadasi we walked round, looking for shoes for Helena and leather coats for Mum. We entered a bakery and saw some pizza looking things, we ordered two and were told to come back in 15 mins, the children did not like them though. Nobody had had enough, so we went to a little restaurant to eat, after that, we went and had an ice cream, a little boy was serving, and he put lots on, it was delicious. We drove on and camped with a lovely view of the town.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Photo of Kusadasi from camp. Visit to Aphrodias. Fantastic! Great piles of ?? ?? etc everywhere.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Photo outside ?? ?? housing relics and photo of ??

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage 30892 (3292 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Photo of stone wheel and tent on ??. 2 photos with D’s camera, of Dobby donkeys

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage 30910 (3310 miles travelled). Pammukale - Super! Spent night in graveyard.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove to Pammukale, and we could see nothing out of the ordinary, until we rounded a bend, and there it was, a whole mountainside of white pools, overflowing into each other, and making beautiful patterns. On the top of the mountain were the remains of a large, Roman city. We went swimming in a pool with a Motel round it. It was body temperature with lots of bubbles coming up, it looked and tasted like soda water. It had lots of old pillars, and stones under water, it was like the old ruins outside. I swam under three columns.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Pammukale. It is famous for its warm springs and limestone formations. First, the Greeks then the Romans, then the Turks came there. In one motel they had made a pool with lots of Roman columns and things in. It was lovely and warm. I swam under a column with the goggles on but they slipped off and I had to shut my eyes because the limestone water stung my eyes. I also swam under two rocks, once with goggles, twice without. The Romans used to have crocodiles with which the gladiators used to fight. The Romans also built a theatre which could hold about 15000 people. It was the third best Roman Theatre in the world. They were still excavating when we went. There was a very big Roman cemetery.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to Pammukale. There are some hot lime springs. They taste like soda. There are ruins in some hot water swimming pools. We went swimming twice and saw pillars which were covered with sticking out lines. I fans, “skill, skill”! did a somersault into the water. My dives are improving. We went to some sulphur springs - they were very very very hot.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage 31074 (3473 miles travelled) - Camped between Is?? and Antalya

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, we found we had been sleeping in a Roman graveyard. F and H saw a ghost. We drove up and saw a Roman Amphitheatre it was very big, but men were still working on cleaning it. After, we went to find the hot sulphur springs. When we found them, they were very hot. They weren’t white, but a deep reddish-brown because of the different chemical properties of the water.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to some sulphur springs near Pammukale. They were very, very hot and made almost everything red. There were lots of little bits of minerals that crunched under foot. Some people were sulphering a pot then. We went to paddle in some limestone pools, then we had a last swim. We lent our goggles to a French speaking Turk. He was the Commander of 4 tanks, 24 people. He invited us to tea and gave us some peach juice.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: The sulphur bubbles up from the ground. I jump onto some firm looking ground but it gave way and I found myself in boiling water. I really got burnt. The water made reddish-brown deposits on the rocks.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Cornfield new Aspendos.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We’ve seen lots of goats round our campsite. Went to Antalya, it was very hot. We had a drink overlooking the harbour, and then some delicious ice cream. We then drove on to Lara beach where we swam. Then we drove to see the Aspendos Amphitheatre, it looked like a big house, perhaps 200 years old from the front, but inside was a big sweep of seats around a stage, the acoustics were superb.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: At Aspendos, I thought that the outside was just a big house, but when we went in I found out that it was an amphitheatre. The best preserved in the World. Me and H went almost everywhere we could. Helena sand the dream scene in Fiddler on the Roof. There was one bit of a rock that made a super slide. It was a metre fall at the end. After that we went.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to Aspendos. From the outside it looks like a castle. It is really an amphitheatre. I went to every passage - secret or not - that I could get to. The seats were hollow. There was a passage underneath which went right to(?) the theatre. It was much nicer than the ruined city.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: (from 1 March) In Aspendos, I found some treasure and a secret passage. In ‘Side’ I found 12 likely places for Denise and I to find some treasure. In Alanya, Denise and I found 8 likely places for treasure to be hidden.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 31250 (3650 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Mum & Dads Wedding Anniversary

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: On Sunday, a little boy stole our bag of peaches.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We found quite a nice campsite under a pine tree on some straw stubble. Some men came while we were having dinner, we gave them some soup and grapes. We went to see Side, there was a ruined city with an amphitheatre, there was also some public lavatories (Roman ones). We went to see a museum as well, it was in an old building, part of it was a super bathroom.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went to Alanya, and after looking for dresses etc, we went to a Restaurant and tried some delicious new things there.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: As we were driving along the sea we came to a ruined city. We stopped under some trees, there was a small circular temple. Nearby stood an amphitheatre. It had been shaken by earthquakes. I found an earthquake-made passage that came between some seats. I called out - Dad was really surprised. In the end, he helped me out. There were some mosaics. In the stage, there were lots of marble pieces. I found some carved theatre masks and a lion. Dad took a photo of a theatre mask.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to “Side”. We have been to Alanya and visited a castle. It was sunny and Horable (sic).

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went out to dinner at a restaurant because it was Mum and Dad’s 13th wedding anniversary. I got lost but an English lady took me to the kitchen where the others were. Then we had dinner and an ice cream. It was by the sea, gourds hung down from the roof. It was lovely.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped on a beach, right next to the sea, just out of Alanya. It was lovely and sandy, but when we got up at 1.00 at night to have a swim, we discovered that in the water, it was all rocky, there were some big breakers, we just stood in the waves. In the morning there were lorries everywhere, filing up with sand. We went back to Alanya to visit a castle, it was 800’ high on a mountain jutting out from the coastline, its outside walls were 5 miles long in all, it was really almost a little city, with 400 water cisterns, public baths and a mosque, it was restored in 13th century AD by the Seljuks.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: At Alanya, we went to the Castle. It was very big and old. The walls were all crenellated and altogether five miles long. In the 13th century, it was rebuilt by the Seljuks. We went to the Sultan’s Palace - it led to a tower and along the wall. We went in two cisterns they used to keep water. One was bigger than the other. Both had stalactites. It was quite dark but not horribly dark. The roof was supported by arches. It was about 10’ by 18’. You could see the old water level by marks on the pillars.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to Anamur. We climbed a high circular tower. Most were square but this one wasn’t. The bottom was a prison. The sea was very blue and the walls thick.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I woke up and had breakfast then I got dressed and went to Alanya. I had an ice cream. In the evening, we went to a castle. Anamun Castle - Denise and I climbed a very high round tower. It had a middle pillar which was fairly solid till we came to the third stair.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage 31378 (3778 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped in a camping place near the sea, we found a raft on the beach, and after some struggling, got it afloat, it just took our weight, but we got the impression that it wasn’t really designed for a life on the ocean waves!

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove for quite a long time through some beautiful scenery, mostly along the coast. We stopped to get some fruit and bought some dried, sweet things, they looked like dried bananas, but have big pips, like this (diagram here). (15/6/21 - sounds like carob beans).

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We were driving by the coast. The sea was a nice blue with white streaks. We didn’t see any boats. There was an area with All Stopping Prohibited and No Cameras or Filming (pic). We went on further and there was a junction but one road said Prohibited Area. Later I saw a Radar station.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we started to look for a campsite. At last we found one. Helena, D and I went to the beach. We made an aquarium in a pool with some camouflaged fish. We put in two black and seven purple urchins. Helena got some spikes in her foot. D piggy-backed her back and we had spaghetti napolitana then we did our diaries. I suddenly saw a face. I thought it was the farmer and told Dad then the man asked if we were German or English and said that he came from control

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been driving all day and are trying to find a camping spot. Then we decide to camp at a campsite near the sea. There were cold showers and some changing rooms. We parked in some pine trees. There were some good tables. We drove along a very windy road, sometimes we were next to the sea, and sometimes on high mountains. The sea was a bit darker and greener than turquoise.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 31527 (3927 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Went to see some caves called “Heaven & Hell”. There was also an ‘asthma-curing cave’. They used to throw sinners down into Hell. We went to see Hell first, it has a chasm, 120m deep, and we counted about 6 secs for a stone to fall, that was with a watch, we all made it about 10 secs counting though. Heaven was another chasm but we could walk down into it. There was an old chapel, and behind it, a large cave, at the end there was an underwater stream. Unfortunately we didn’t go right in to the asthma cave, it looked good though. We had a nice stop at a sandy beach.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Last night, we came to a BP Mocamp. It had a small playground and a shop and lots of trees and bushes plus a cooking place and washing up. Had a shower.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: At 9 o’clock in the morning, we visited Hell which is a deep pit. In the olden days, the sinners were thrown down there. Then we visited Heaven, which was a deep valley. Goatsneck which is a kind of tree, grew there. Near the bottom there was a small Roman chapel near the mouth of a very big dark spooky cave. In the afternoon the roof rack broke.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 31672 (4072 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Today we left the coast, and went inland. We saw some nomads, they had camels and donkeys, also horses and sheep. In the afternoon we went to see some underground cities, they were big places but lots of the passages we went through were small. It was very interesting. We had the guide who took ‘Blue Peter’ [UK kids program on BBC] round a few years ago.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to an underground city. It was very cold. They used millstones to shut the door. It was used as a hideout. You could even keep animals in there.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to an underground city. There were lots of very small passages. There were also some big millstones which were used to stop enemies getting in. We were guided round by a nice guide who had 7 children and had guided the people from blue peter round. (Pic)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We arrived in a BP Mocamp, very nice. Pitched tent H & I slept in it. In the morning, we went to Goreme. There were lots of churches carved out of the rocks, and places where the monks and nuns lived. It was super climbing up to the places.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Went to Goreme. (pic) On the way we stopped and I grazed my knee and had a bandage put on. Then we went to see some churches. They were hollowed out of rocks with murals on.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We saw lots of churches which were cut in some rocks, the shape of ice cream cones upside down. When we saw a picture of St George, I thought he looked rather smug.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Visited Avenos. Bought 3 large bowls, 3 small bowls. Visited Zelve. Spent night Chez Ali at Ortohisar(?). Rather disappointing. Ali ?? ?? ?? tried to talk. No-one else could.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We left the Mocamp and drove to Ortahisar, in the middle of the small town was a big rock, that had been hollowed out into to passages and small rooms, we climbed to the top and had a super view of the surrounding countryside, and we could see lots of apricots etc drying on the roofs. When we came down we met a man who took us to his house to see some carpet making. He then invited us to stay the night at his house. We accepted and said that we’d come at about 6.00 that night. We drove off and went to visit Avanos. There, we visited onyx and pottery shops and saw men making things. I bought a little onyx goblet, and bargained down to 15tL (45p) from 20tL (60p). Then we went to a pottery shop. We saw a man making lots of cups. I bought a small one for 12p instead of 15p. Then we went to see more ‘rock ruins’ at Zelve. When we came back to the Turkish house, we sat round, drinking Chai and talking - or trying to. At last we got to bed, and although nice to sleep in a house the mattresses weren’t all that comfy.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Zelve and parked Fred then we read til four. At four, we got out and started walking through a valley. There was a dried up river. We split up, the girls went along the riverbed. Me and Dad walked higher up in the rocks. Then Dad saw a church. It had a crack in the roof and two walls were missing. I found a pass into another valley. We went through and found that we could get in the church. Dad took a photo. We found a ladder leading to a dark room with a passage to a window at the end. Then I found another room with a tunnel to a window. It was about eighty feet down. Then we went back. It was amazing how much more our eyes could see. We then went back to the pass and went back to the river bed because there was a huge cave, only Dad, me and H went in. There were millions of tunnels and chimneys, rooms, and windows. We weren’t allowed much time. Then we got out and left.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the evening, we went to a Turkish man’s house. We were all given some chai. They had a big flat roof where they were drying lots of onions and apricots. There were also some unshelled almonds there - and found that if you smash the pip of an apricot there is a kernel in it.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Then we went to a town and Denise bought something. It was the shape of an eggcup but it was very small and made of onyx.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 31815 (4215 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Went to Kayseri where we met a student who took us round. There was a big high mountain behind, that was capped in snow. We drove on, and the land was very dry.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: At Kaysery (sic), we visited a carpet shop. When we went in, the carpets were in rolls against the walls. The man who owned the shop got lots of carpets down but we did not want them. We liked three of them but did not buy one. They were all dyed with vegetable dyes, some of the carpets were wool or wool and cotton, and silk ones. The carpets are made with lots of knots, but Kelims are woven. I liked the silk carpets because they were so fine and shiny. I also liked the wool ones because they are so soft.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 31972 (4372 miles travelled). Slept outside Malataya near small dam.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped in the middle of nowhere, there was a very cold wind, we woke up in the morning surrounded by a thick mist.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stopped for lunch by a small river, on the other side of the river was a foal and a beautiful horse, eating grass, they were in a little glade, with an oval patch of flowers behind them, they were against the sun so we couldn’t capture their beauty in a photograph. Some children came with some older boys, who had a gun, one spoke a little French but it was difficult getting on with them.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We left the misty mountain and started driving. It was not asphalt, then it became asphalt. There was a meandering stream that literally was like this (pic). Then we saw some soldiers digging a hole. Then we saw a soldier sitting down and two pulling wire. They were setting up a communications line.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We stopped for lunch near a river, it was deep and fast flowing. Some boys and girls came and watched. The eldest boy had a gun, he fired it twice. We then went onto the road again.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: At five o’clock we stopped at a patch of ground near a pond that irrigated the nearby fields. There were trees on one side of us and sand on the other. H and I made a dam and a stream round it. Then D came and we made small fountains. Then we breached the dam.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the evening, we stopped by a pool which had a stream from an underground spring. Francis and I built a dam with a stream running round it. The dam was made of stones and mud and the stream which ran round was quite ??

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 32134 (4534 miles travelled). Crossed Firat ie Euphrates.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped near a little spring, and had fun daming the little stream, and changing its course. We found some hollow reeds, and made some small fountains.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, three children came, two boys and a little girl. We gave them some pencils and paper, and they bought us some big tomatoes. It’s twelve o’clock and I’m sitting, writing, in a little covered place with tables and benches, with walls of hanging ‘Morning Glory’ in front of a little garden with some beautiful flowers, needless to say, it all surrounds a spring.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: In the morning, while we were eating breakfast, two boys and a girl came. We gave them some pencils and paper, they gave us tomatoes. The pool reflected trees and things very well. It had some water beetles in it. There were lots of flowers and birds here.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We had lunch at a lovely garden. It had a verandah that had got string hanging from the roof with morning glorys growing up it. Their coils were light pink.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 32261 (4661 miles travelled). Night just after Bitlis. Had ?? to Jandarme .. so pestered by shepherds, women etc.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Postcard to Erica & Nathalie(?)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Last night we made a bivouac in a little hollow, there were lots of oak-bushes and with some wood we propped up a roof. We had spaghetti for dinner and Helena spilt hers, and burnt her tummy, in the morning she was alright though, she also wet her bed, I think through shock.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Lots of goats came, while we were eating breakfast, Helena and Francis were having theirs in the bivouac, and were soon surrounded, it was OK though. We drove to Lake Van, the people weren’t very friendly, and some boys threw stones at us, and hit. In a town, there was a fight, luckily, we weren’t in the middle of it. When at long last, we found a stop, (near a Police station) we were quickly surrounded by people, it was very difficult eating in front of them. We didn’t have enough though, for all all of them. In the end, Mum and F went and got the Police, the people went away, but we drove Fred to the station, just in case.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: The place where we stopped was full of oak trees. There was a dell that had a wall on one side and in the rest gentle or steep slope. We propped up some sticks with rocks and made a roof (pic). Then H and I found two tortoises. We carried them 400 yards. They got their photo taken. (pic)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 32441 (4841 miles travelled). At van. Stayed at Dinleme Jandarme Kampi v.good.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went into Van itself, and had lunch in a Restaurant that a man in the tourist information recommended to us. It was very nice, the first place where everyone liked the food. Then we went to the museum, it had lots of different and old writing. (diagram here). Then we went down to the sea where there was a great outcrop of rock with the ruins of an old castle on it. I finished the film of the camera, taking a shot of Mum and a tower. The castle was basically stone with mud bricks on top, the mud had kept very well, for over 2000 years. We went back into Van, and bought a new film for the camera. Then we went to a Jandarma place, there was a beach, we swam, but it was very cold. We had chai with the soldiers, and played ‘Liar dice’. [Jandarma is a Turkish Police Station where you can camp.]

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Van. It was very big and modern. There was a Museum. It had some nice ?? and glass work as well as pottery and some nice gold work.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to a Jarndarma camping. )) MB Jarndarma Might be a french word??? MB It had a lighthouse on a rock (pic). We cleared it of cobwebs and made it cleaner. It was in a wooden box. There was some space left that we filled with marble almost up to the windows it had had in it but it was broken so a soldier threw it away into the sea.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the afternoon, we went to a Jandarma which had a model lighthouse with a broken bulb and a red top. The bulb did not work and had a hole in the top. The lighthouse was white and placed in the middle of a blue wooden box. It had a staircase going up the outside. The inside was hollow except for the light workings(?). Francis and I cleaned the lighthouse with Denise. We filled the box with marble from a heap of it.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We just stayed in one place today, and did washing & things, found two mice, one dead and one dying. We also found two pairs of butterflies wings. We walked to a village to get some shopping but it was much farther than we thought.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We did a three kilometre walk to the shops. It was a windy road near the sea. There were lots of flies. We bought some bread and grapes then we came back. Dad and I did some exploring and found lots of frogs.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We walked to Edremit. It was a three kilometre walk there. At the shops we bought bread and fruit. On the way back, we saw a dead squirrel. Dad and Francis found some frogs.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Took lots of photos of monastery at Aktamar.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went on a boat trip to the island with two Germans, to visit an old monastery. Armenian with interesting carvings of men and animals. We went in a small old motor boat, the sea was a very beautiful colour. In the afternoon, despite the strong, cold wind, we had a swim, the sea was very choppy.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to a monastery, it was on an island. On one church there were lots of nice carvings of things like people and animals. We took some photos. There were some pigeons eggs and nests. It was very windy. The monastery was in ruins. I liked it. It was Armenian and 1000 years old.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: On Sunday, we went to an island. It had a monastery on it. Only pigeons live in it now. On the outside there were carvings of saints and animals. The boat was small and painted white, blue and red. The water was a nice shade of green on the way there but blue on the way back.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 32502 (4902 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we got up, Dad and I went for an early morning swim. It was very windy outside, but the water wasn’t too bad. We said goodbye to the Corporal and Private, and then set off on the road to IRAN. The first bit was asphalt, and quite good, but then we came to some roadworks, where it was practically non-existent, from there on we had to go slowly, bumping along, but it meant we saw more. Mummy saw an eagle, so we stopped and took some photos. We also saw some smaller, very brightly coloured birds, we thought they were relatives of the Kingfishers. We found a dead one on the road, it was very beautiful. When we got to the Border, after all the customs, we slept, just on the Iranian side.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: On the way to Iran, we saw some small birds. They were like kingfishers and had very bright colours. We took some photos. Once when we stopped, someone thought that we had an accident but really we were taking a photo. Then we took some photos of eagles - they were huge. It was a very bumpy road. Suddenly we had a blowout - the tyre went bang and we stopped. Helena, Denise and I went to a river. H picked some perfect, posh, purple peppermints then we came back. Soon after we crossed the border and stopped in Iran.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the afternoon we had a blowout. While Dad changed the tyre, Denise, Francis and I went down to the river. I found lots of purple peppermint flowers.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: That evening we crossed the frontier into Iran and camped at the border.
